review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Rule-governed game activities, sports by equipment and team format, physical exercise, and physical game equipment. Separate cards as activity from playing cards as objects.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Cambridge, Collins and BWF support terminology and selected scope corrections. Definitions are not copied; graph mappings and restrictions are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Game activity, physical equipment, intended use and playing format remain separate. Social interaction and bodily action are not mutually exclusive. Sport is not universally classified as physical exercise; its existing scope includes chess.

sense_decisions.scope: A game activity structured by rules; select the activity sense rather than equipment, hunted animals, a match result or musical performance. Do not require gambling or competition between multiple players.

A game organized around a designated game board and its positions. The mechanics can be represented physically or digitally; this activity is not a wooden board, equipment set or a generic game on a sports field.
A rule-governed game using tiles as playing units, including a digital representation of those units. A rigid game board is not required.
The overlap of sports activity and rule-governed game activity. Do not identify every form of sport, physical exercise or informal play with this restricted family.
Sport played in opposing teams. The selected format concerns the competing sides in play, not a club affiliation or a tournament team made up of singles players.
Sporting games using a ball. Broaden the dictionary field-only wording to include court and table sports; exclude a shuttlecock and a hockey puck.
Sporting games played with rackets, including table-tennis rackets. Not all rackets have strings and not all racket sports use a ball.
The racket game using a shuttlecock, distinct from tennis and from a ball-game family. No scoring system or equipment regulation is encoded.
The game using rackets and a small ball across a table. It is a racket sport and a ball sport, not a subtype of lawn tennis.
The racket-and-ball game, not a vegetable, plant, drink or crushing action.
Tennis with a pair of players on each side. This is a team format without claiming that every form of tennis is a team sport.
Tennis with one player on each side. A singles match may still count toward a wider team competition; no blanket social or event exclusion is asserted.
Badminton with a pair of players on each side. Do not import bare doubles as an unambiguous synonym.
Badminton with one player on each side. This format remains distinct from the type of tournament or club membership.
Table tennis played by a pair on each side. No service order, scoring rule or equipment specification is asserted.
Physical artifacts intended for play or games. Broaden organized-game wording to include informal play; an equipment item is not the game activity itself.
A ball intended for sport, also belonging to sports equipment. Not every ball is a toy, sporting item or geometrically exact sphere.
A ball designed as a toy. This preserves the legitimate overlap without making every sporting ball a toy.
A racket for striking a ball or shuttlecock in a racket game. Strings are common but not universal; include the solid striking surface of a table-tennis racket.
A racket intended for tennis; no frame material, size or string specification is asserted.
A racket intended for badminton; historical battledore meanings are not automatically imported.
The racket, paddle or bat used in table tennis. Use the selected sports-racket family; it need not have strings.
A racket intended for squash. Do not import the bare bat synonym, which has other sports and animal senses.
The badminton projectile, with a base and drag-producing skirt. Allow feathered and synthetic constructions; do not require natural feathers or classify it as a ball.
A ball intended for tennis; no particular material, pressure or dimension is asserted.
The light hollow ball intended for table tennis; do not prescribe a material or current competition dimensions.
A ball intended for association football, not every regional football-code ball.
The physical ball used in basketball, distinct from the existing basketball activity.
The physical ball used in volleyball, distinct from the existing volleyball activity.
A physical card intended for card games. Move the old equipment label off the activity record. Do not import maps, circuit cards or a fixed deck size.
A physical tile used as a playing unit, distinct from the activity or a software representation.
The physical domino playing piece. Do not limit every set to double-six values or import the mask and cloak homonyms.
A physical game board rather than the activity, electronic circuit, governing committee or generic timber plank.
The physical board intended for chess; not a chess game or a software-rendered board.
Bodily exercise performed for practice or physical conditioning. It is a kind of exercise and physical action, not every bodily motion and not necessarily competitive sport.

sense_decisions.alignment: exercise scope wider than competitive discipline
sense_decisions.scope: Physical exercises involving gymnastic movement and control. Competition is not required, and no therapeutic outcome or exercise instructions are asserted.
The existing play root also has musical and verb-generated descendants. Reuse it as the broad play anchor but add a narrower rule-game family instead of equating all senses.
The existing sport family includes chess. Do not import a universal physical-exertion genus from the narrower dictionary gloss.
Athletics can mean sport broadly or track and field more narrowly. Do not create an identity or new children until the existing Russian athletics record is qualified.
Existing cycling selects bicycle sport. Do not import motorcycle racing or generic bicycle travel from wider cycling usages.
Mountaineering is narrower than generic climbing. Preserve this for a separate activity/sport review.
Reuse the play/sport ball, distinct from a geometrical ball, dance event or other spherical object.
Competition is reused later for events; do not make every sport activity a particular competition event.

review.limits: No competition regulations, fixed scores, dimensions, deck sizes, player eligibility, exercise prescription or health outcome. Board, card and tile game families describe game mechanics and do not require every occurrence to use physical equipment. Equipment concepts explicitly select physical artifacts. Musical play, sports event/discipline scope, athletics/track-and-field, general swimming versus vessels, mountaineering/climbing, skiing and the remaining generated action names need further review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Reject the false gymnastics/sport and social/physical-action exclusions, and the sport/play exclusion before adding reviewed game/sport intersections. Retain both genus families and leave other exclusions untouched.

new_term_collisions.decision: Reviewed move: remove the object label from card-game activity before attaching it to the physical-card sense.

review.collision_decision: One exact collision is a reviewed label move from card-game activity to physical playing cards. All other new names and aliases have no exact normalized cross-language match. Existing games, sport disciplines, balls, card artifacts and sports equipment are reused.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
